task_3_extended_interview.title: Dr. Julian Croft: Subterranean Speleology
task_3_extended_interview.instruction: Listen to the interview and answer questions 3–7. (2 plays maximum)

questions.stem: 3. What originally drew Julian from mountaineering to submerged cave diving?

options.label: [A] The chance to test experimental diving suits in deep waters
[B] The total absence of pre-existing maps in unexplored submerged chambers
[C] The desire to break international cave depth records

questions.trap: Irresistible pull: sheer absence of pre-existing maps in submerged labyrinths.

questions.stem: 4. According to Julian, what was the most physically and mentally exhausting trial underground?

options.label: [A] Calculating gas supply volumes on closed-circuit rebreathers
[B] Squeezing blind through ultra-narrow limestone silt restrictions
[C] Enduring prolonged sub-zero temperatures in subterranean water pools

questions.trap: Navigating ultra-narrow silt restrictions blind without kicking up limestone.

questions.stem: 5. What crucial scientific fact did finding giant ground sloth skeletons reveal?

options.label: [A] The flooded cave labyrinth had once been dry inland valleys during the ice age
[B] Prehistoric human settlements maintained domesticated megafauna inside caves
[C] Sea level rise occurred much more recently than previously documented

questions.trap: Sloth fossils inland prove cave systems were bone-dry valleys during glacial maximum.

questions.stem: 6. Why are pharmaceutical scientists keen to analyze the cave's bacterial colonies?

options.label: [A] They consume microplastics and industrial toxins in water supplies
[B] They produce unique antimicrobial compounds effective against drug-resistant superbugs
[C] They synthesize renewable biofuels through chemoautotrophic metabolism

questions.trap: Synthesize unique antimicrobial compounds potent against hospital superbugs.

questions.stem: 7. What fundamental guidance does Julian impart to aspiring exploratory researchers?

options.label: [A] Invest in the latest autonomous mapping drones before mounting an expedition
[B] Prioritize instinctive wilderness competence over technological instruments
[C] Never conduct field dives without constant satellite telemetry links

questions.trap: Prioritize intuitive rock reading and staying calm over digital tools.

task_3_extended_interview.title: Naomi Chen: Glacial Acoustic Ecology
task_3_extended_interview.instruction: Listen to the interview and answer questions 3–7. (2 plays maximum)

questions.stem: 3. What inspired Naomi to transition from classical percussion to soundscape ecology?

options.label: [A] A childhood fascination with deep-sea whale acoustics
[B] Recognizing that measuring natural acoustic balance is a sensitive diagnostic of ecosystem health
[C] Growing frustrated with commercial orchestra competition

questions.trap: Acoustic balance proved the most sensitive diagnostic tool for ecosystem vitality.

questions.stem: 4. What was the most difficult acoustic challenge Naomi’s team encountered in Patagonia?

options.label: [B] Low-frequency infrasound turbulence generated by katabatic winds
[C] Intense background animal vocalizations overloading recorders

questions.trap: Katabatic winds roaring off ice sheet generate extreme infrasound turbulence.

questions.stem: 5. How does sub-surface acoustic monitoring evaluate glacier stability better than satellites?

options.label: [A] It measures the exact mineral salinity of subglacial meltwater
[B] It detects micro-fracture acoustic bursts days before surface fissures appear from orbit
[C] It accurately maps the thickness of accumulated seasonal snowfall

questions.trap: Acoustic micro-fracture bursts forecast structural collapse days before surface rifts.

questions.stem: 6. What alarmed Naomi regarding the acoustic monitoring of high-altitude bird species?

options.label: [A] Birds migrating northward earlier than historical averages
[B] The rapid acoustic homogenization and collapse of vocal frequency diversity
[C] Invasive species mimicking the calls of native songbirds

questions.trap: Rapid acoustic homogenization: intricate counterpoint collapses into monoculture.

questions.stem: 7. How does Naomi recommend engaging the public on environmental degradation?

options.label: [A] Releasing raw numerical decibel spreadsheets to schools
[B] Immersing listeners directly in the visceral sounds of dying habitats
[C] Commissioning pop musicians to sample wildlife calls

questions.trap: Immerse ears directly in soundscape; groan of dying glacier cuts through apathy.

task_3_extended_interview.title: Rachel Vance • Cold-Chain Logistics
task_3_extended_interview.instruction: You will hear an interview with Rachel Vance, operations director for a nationwide cold-chain distribution network. (2 plays maximum)

questions.stem: 3. What first attracted Rachel to cold-chain distribution rather than standard dry warehousing?

options.label: [A] The financial incentives offered by international pharmaceutical shippers
[B] The rigorous operational precision required by strict temperature tolerances
[C] The ability to avoid unpredictable transit delays on regional motorways

questions.trap: [A] finances not stated; [C] delays happen and are critical.

questions.stem: 4. Rachel explains that the main hurdle with electric refrigerated delivery lorries is:

options.label: [A] The heavy power drain of cooling compressors during hot weather congestion
[B] The unreliability of vehicle propulsion batteries in sub-zero winter temperatures
[C] The shortage of high-voltage charging points at regional customer delivery sites

questions.trap: [B] propulsion works well; [C] compressor draw during heatwaves is the stated issue.

questions.stem: 5. How did warehouse automation at the Northampton facility affect floor workers?

options.label: [A] It forced management to reduce total employee numbers by a third.
[B] It enabled staff to transition from heavy manual lifting to robotics supervision.
[C] It caused widespread dissatisfaction due to increased hourly picking quotas.

questions.trap: [A] headcount remained stable; [C] dissatisfaction not reported.

questions.stem: 6. How does Rachel's team manage sudden spikes in supermarket grocery demand?

options.label: [A] By purchasing excess safety stock based on previous seasonal sales data
[B] By combining real-time checkout telemetry with regional weather forecasts
[C] By requiring retail stores to submit delivery requisitions a week in advance

questions.trap: [A] historical averages explicitly rejected; [C] real-time 24h rebalancing used.

questions.stem: 7. What advice does Rachel impart to graduates entering the supply chain sector?

options.label: [A] Focus immediately on mastering executive data analytics software.
[B] Gain practical experience on loading bays and depot floors first.
[C] Seek management opportunities exclusively with international freight carriers.

questions.trap: [A] warns against staying behind dashboards in head office.

task_3_extended_interview.title: David Cho • Sustainable Consumer Hardware
task_3_extended_interview.instruction: You will hear an interview with industrial designer David Cho regarding repairable domestic appliances. (2 plays maximum)

questions.stem: 3. Why did David leave traditional consumer electronics manufacturing?

options.label: [A] Frustration with adhesive construction that forced premature product disposal

[C] Increasing competition from low-cost overseas assembly factories

questions.trap: [B] adhesives were the issue, not bio-plastics; [C] overseas competition not stated.

questions.stem: 4. What was the greatest engineering hurdle in designing modular appliances?

[C] Reducing the total weight of the modular internal chassis

questions.trap: [B] water ingress was a factor, but standardized modular assembly without bulk was primary.

questions.stem: 5. What unexpected user behavior emerged after the modular appliances were launched?

questions.stem: 6. How does David's company supply spare parts without long shipping waits?

[B] By relying on express international air freight from their central factory
[C] By requiring customers to 3D-print replacement parts in their own homes

questions.trap: [B] air freight explicitly avoided; [C] CAD shared with certified workshops, not home 3D printers.

questions.stem: 7. What does David anticipate will be the main effect of right-to-repair legislation?

options.label: [A] Manufacturers will be forced to compete on durability and ease of repair.

[C] Many smaller electronics companies will struggle to remain financially viable.

questions.trap: [B] build quality improves; prices dropping not stated.

task_6_monologue_gaps.title: Coral Reef Restoration
task_6_monologue_gaps.instruction: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each gap.

questions.stem: 15. Before launching the project, the research team searched for coral colonies with natural _______________________________.
questions.trap: Audio: 'resilient coral colonies that possessed natural thermal tolerance'.

questions.stem: 16. The cutting technique known as micro-fragmentation triggered the corals' _______________________________, accelerating growth rates.
questions.trap: Audio: 'stimulated an innate healing mechanism that accelerated their growth rate'.

questions.stem: 17. Mature fragments were secured onto the ocean floor using a non-toxic _______________________________.
questions.trap: Audio: 'affixed to degraded reef substrates using a non-toxic marine adhesive'.

questions.stem: 18. To control smothering algae, researchers introduced native _______________________________ to act as natural grazers.
questions.trap: Audio: 'we introduced native herbivorous sea urchins, which acted as natural cleaners'.

questions.stem: 19. Dr. Hughes emphasizes that the project's ultimate metric of long-term success is _______________________________ rather than acreage.
questions.trap: Audio: 'true benchmark of our success won't merely be total reef acreage, but genetic diversity'.

task_6_monologue_gaps.title: The Kronan-Nord Baltic Shipwreck
task_6_monologue_gaps.instruction: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each gap.

questions.stem: 15. Ship timbers survived intact due to low water salinity and completely _______________________________, preventing shipworm.
questions.trap: Low salinity and complete anoxic sediments prevent shipworm.

questions.stem: 16. Fragile items in the captain's quarters were cleared using an innovative dredge operated by _______________________________.
questions.trap: Specialized gentle water-dredge operated via controlled hydrostatic suction.

questions.stem: 17. Chemical analysis revealed the pitch was infused with pine resin and _______________________________.
questions.trap: Resinous pitch infused with pine resin and juniper oils.

questions.stem: 18. Recovered waterlogged oak timbers were stabilized by immersion in an aqueous bath of _______________________________.
questions.trap: Aqueous bath of polyethylene glycol synthetic wax displaces trapped water.

questions.stem: 19. The wreck provides rare material proof of undocumented _______________________________ between Scandinavia and the Levant.
questions.trap: Material evidence of undocumented maritime trade networks between Scandinavia and Levant.

questions.stem: 15. Ship timbers survived intact due to low water salinity and completely _______________________________, preventing shipworm.
questions.trap: Low salinity and complete anoxic sediments prevent shipworm.

questions.stem: 16. Fragile items in the captain's quarters were cleared using an innovative dredge operated by _______________________________.
questions.trap: Specialized gentle water-dredge operated via controlled hydrostatic suction.

questions.stem: 17. Chemical analysis revealed the pitch was infused with pine resin and _______________________________.
questions.trap: Resinous pitch infused with pine resin and juniper oils.

questions.stem: 18. Recovered waterlogged oak timbers were stabilized by immersion in an aqueous bath of _______________________________.
questions.trap: Aqueous bath of polyethylene glycol synthetic wax displaces trapped water.

questions.stem: 19. The wreck provides rare material proof of undocumented _______________________________ between Scandinavia and the Levant.
questions.trap: Material evidence of undocumented maritime trade networks between Scandinavia and Levant.

task_6_monologue_gaps.title: Temperate Celtic Rainforests [Track 23]
task_6_monologue_gaps.instruction: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each gap.

questions.stem: 15. Temperate rainforests depend on hyper-humid conditions fostered by the _______________________________.
questions.trap: Hyper-humid microclimates shaped by the Gulf Stream.

questions.stem: 16. Epiphytic lichens are vulnerable because they absorb nutrients straight from _______________________________.
questions.trap: Lack roots and absorb nutrients straight from atmospheric moisture.

questions.stem: 17. Ancient woodland lichens like Sticta are decimated by _______________________________ from traffic and agriculture.
questions.trap: Chronic nitrogen pollution from agricultural runoff and vehicular exhaust.

questions.stem: 18. Natural recolonization across fragmented forests is impeded because many lichens have very _______________________________.
questions.trap: Heavy spores with very limited dispersal radii travelling under 100 meters.

questions.stem: 19. Researchers are trialling _______________________________ to attach small lichen thalli to trees in regenerating corridors.
questions.trap: Trialling micro-translocation strategies: affixing minute lichen thalli to trees.

task_6_monologue_gaps.title: Airport Automated Baggage Handling Systems [Track 24]
task_6_monologue_gaps.instruction: Listen to the briefing on airport automated baggage logistics. Complete each sentence with a word or short phrase from the recording. (2 plays maximum)

questions.stem: 15. Modern luggage tags embed high-frequency [          ] microchips to ensure accurate automated tracking.
questions.trap: Audio: 'RFID microchips embedded alongside traditional barcodes'.

questions.stem: 16. Automated conveyor networks direct bags through 3D [          ] scanners for non-intrusive security inspection.
questions.trap: Audio: 'three-dimensional computed tomography scanners'.

questions.stem: 17. During flight delays, luggage is stored within high-density [          ] facilities instead of open tarmac carts.
questions.trap: Audio: 'dynamic high-density racking facilities'.

questions.stem: 18. Apron electric tug vehicles utilize [          ] sensors to calculate the most efficient transit path to the aircraft.
questions.trap: Audio: 'equipped with telematics sensors that optimize baggage transit'.

questions.stem: 19. The overarching metric of ground handling efficiency is reducing aircraft [          ] time at airport gates.
questions.trap: Audio: 'commercial benchmark of ground logistics efficiency is aircraft turnaround time'.

task_6_monologue_gaps.title: Municipal Wastewater Recycling Infrastructure [Track 25]
task_6_monologue_gaps.instruction: Listen to the presentation on municipal wastewater recycling systems. Complete each sentence with a word or short phrase from the recording. (2 plays maximum)

questions.stem: 15. Incoming wastewater first flows across rotary [          ] screens to extract coarse debris and plastics.
questions.trap: Audio: 'rotary mesh screens to eliminate insoluble plastics'.

questions.stem: 16. Microbial breakdown of organic compounds takes place inside membrane [          ] tanks.
questions.trap: Audio: 'membrane bioreactor chambers, where dense colonies of aerobic microbes'.

questions.stem: 17. During reverse osmosis, dissolved salts are extracted by forcing effluent across [          ] membranes.
questions.trap: Audio: 'through dense polyamide membranes during reverse osmosis'.

questions.stem: 18. The secondary disinfection stage combines ultraviolet light with hydrogen [          ] to destroy lingering impurities.
questions.trap: Audio: 'ultraviolet irradiation combined with hydrogen peroxide'.

questions.stem: 19. The resulting high-grade recycled water is largely supplied to industrial power station [          ] towers.
questions.trap: Audio: 'heavy power station cooling towers, preserving millions of litres'.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Formal Workplace Mediation
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are a team leader in a publishing house. Two senior editors on your team have had a significant professional disagreement regarding the editorial direction of a flagship literary journal, causing delays in publication. Write an email to your department head explaining the root cause of the friction, summarizing the mediation steps you have undertaken, and proposing a compromise schedule to ensure the journal meets its deadline.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Academic Conference Grant Report
task_1_narrative.prompt: You recently received a travel grant from your university's academic research board to present a paper at an international linguistics symposium. Write a formal report to the grant committee summarizing your paper's reception, detailing two significant methodological insights gained from peer discussions, and outlining how this experience will enrich your department's upcoming seminar series.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Facilities Disruption Compensation
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are the manager of an independent co-working space. Unexpected plumbing and electrical renovations forced the temporary closure of the primary meeting suites for four days, disrupting several client presentations. Write a professional letter to all registered members explaining the structural emergency, offering appropriate commercial compensation, and detailing preventative maintenance upgrades underway.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Heritage Site Advisory Proposal
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are an assistant conservation officer at a regional archaeological site. Recent surges in tourist foot traffic have caused noticeable erosion to ancient sandstone staircases and masonry. Write a formal proposal to the regional heritage director recommending two visitor-flow management solutions and outlining a community volunteer monitoring program.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Clinical Trial Participant Recalibration
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are the head coordinator for a clinical trial investigating a new nutritional supplement. Due to updated ethical guidelines from the institutional review board, participant monitoring protocols must be modified. Write a clear, reassuring letter to study participants explaining the updated appointment frequency and addressing potential privacy concerns.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: University Exchange Program Evaluation
task_1_narrative.prompt: You have recently completed a semester abroad at a partner university under an academic exchange scholarship. Write a formal evaluation letter to the international relations office outlining the academic benefits, identifying logistical challenges encountered with housing, and suggesting improvements for incoming cohorts.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Municipal Eco-Audit Recommendation
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are an environmental consultant hired by a district council to audit commercial energy waste in civic administrative complexes. Write an executive summary memorandum to the council president highlighting two major sources of thermal inefficiency and proposing a phased retrofitting strategy.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Museum Exhibition Loan Negotiation
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are a curator at a regional historical museum planning a centenary exhibition on industrial maritime history. Write a formal loan request letter to the keeper of collections at a national maritime museum requesting the display loan of three original shipwright blueprints, explaining security measures and climate controls in place.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Laboratory Equipment Relocation
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are a senior laboratory technician at a bioscience research institute. Due to ventilation duct maintenance, two specialized centrifuges must be temporarily moved to Basement Room B-12 next Monday. Write an email to all lab personnel explaining the schedule, noting safety precautions for hazardous sample transport, and providing booking instructions for alternative equipment.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Community Arts Center Workshop Feedback
task_1_narrative.prompt: You organized a weekend woodcarving workshop at a local community center. Write a formal summary letter to the center's program director detailing attendee participation, highlighting constructive feedback regarding workshop ventilation and tool storage, and suggesting two improvements for the autumn program.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: University Library Study Pod Reservation Issue
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are the student representative for postgraduate researchers. Frequent software errors in the library study pod booking system have resulted in double bookings and lost study hours. Write a formal letter to the chief university librarian detailing the recurring technical failures, explaining the impact on thesis completion, and recommending an interim solution.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Public Transportation Route Disruption Advisory
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are a customer communications officer for a municipal tram network. Urgent track replacement will suspend tram service between Central Station and East Wharf for two weeks. Write a passenger notice explaining the maintenance necessity, detailing replacement bus shuttle frequencies, and outlining season ticket reimbursement procedures.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Ecological Habitat Restoration Volunteer Briefing
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are the coordinator of a wetlands conservation charity. You have organized a Saturday volunteer planting day along the tidal estuary. Write an orientation email to registered volunteers outlining the rendezvous point, mandatory protective clothing requirements, tool allocation, and safety precautions regarding tidal currents.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Office Renewable Energy Transition Memo
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are the sustainability officer for an architectural firm. The firm is transitioning its regional headquarters to one hundred percent rooftop solar power this month. Write an internal memorandum to all staff explaining the installation timeline, advising on temporary parking bay closures, and describing new smart lighting controls.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Historic Town Hall Guided Tour Review
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are a heritage officer who recently audited the weekend guided tour experience at the historic town hall. Write a report to the municipal cultural affairs committee commending the historical accuracy of the guides, identifying accessibility bottlenecks for wheelchair users, and suggesting multilingual audio guide additions.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Medical Clinic Patient Appointment System Update
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are the practice manager of a busy community medical clinic. The clinic is launching an updated digital patient portal for prescription renewals and routine check-up bookings. Write a clear advisory notice for patients explaining the benefits of the new platform, reassuring elderly patients about telephone booking availability, and providing registration steps.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: International Student Orientation Welcome & Guide
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are the student welfare coordinator at a regional college. A new cohort of sixty international exchange students will arrive next week. Write a welcoming orientation letter explaining airport transfer options, student identity card pickup procedures, and mandatory campus health center registration.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Culinary School Kitchen Appliance Upgrade Request
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are the head chef instructor at a vocational culinary academy. Several commercial induction ranges in the main training kitchen are malfunctioning, compromising practical exam schedules. Write a formal procurement proposal to the academy dean justifying the immediate replacement with energy-efficient models and providing an estimated budget.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Botanical Garden Rare Orchid Exhibition Notice
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are the chief horticulturist at a metropolitan botanical garden. A rare tropical orchid is set to bloom for only forty-eight hours in the glasshouse pavilion. Write a public advisory notice explaining the botanical rarity, outlining extended evening visiting hours, and emphasizing photography guidelines with tripod restrictions.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: University Sports Complex Renovation Notice
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are the administrative manager of the campus athletic facilities. The Olympic swimming pool and fitness suite will close for three weeks in August for filtration system overhauls. Write an email to all registered gym members explaining the structural improvements, outlining reciprocal access agreements with neighboring facilities, and detailing automatic membership fee freezes.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Neighborhood Clean Air Zone Consultation Summary
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are an environmental policy analyst working for an urban borough council. You have completed a public consultation regarding a proposed low-emission vehicle zone. Write an executive summary memorandum to the borough mayor summarizing residents' support for cleaner air, addressing local shopkeepers' concerns regarding delivery access, and proposing delivery loading exemptions.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Freelance Graphic Designer Scope Revision Letter
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are a freelance creative director commissioned to design a brand identity for a local organic food cooperative. Mid-way through the project, the client requested three additional animated promotional videos not included in the original agreement. Write a professional letter explaining the additional time requirements, outlining a revised milestone schedule, and presenting a transparent supplemental fee structure.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Youth Apprenticeship Program Mentorship Report
task_1_narrative.prompt: You coordinate a vocational apprenticeship initiative connecting high school graduates with regional manufacturing workshops. Write an interim report to the regional employment board highlighting apprentice retention rates, detailing feedback from master toolmakers, and recommending expanded technical drawing tutorials.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Campus Bicycle Fleet Maintenance Announcement
task_1_narrative.prompt: You manage the student union shared bicycle initiative. Over the winter break, all eighty fleet bicycles will undergo comprehensive brake and gear refurbishments. Write a notice to student users explaining the scheduled return deadline for bicycles, outlining the penalties for overdue returns, and previewing the newly added electronic locking stations.

task_1_narrative.title: Task 1: Corporate Charity 10K Run Sponsorship Appeal
task_1_narrative.prompt: You are the corporate social responsibility coordinator for an engineering enterprise. Your office is entering a team into the annual charity run to support a regional youth hospice. Write an engaging email to all department heads encouraging employee participation, explaining corporate donation matching, and providing registration links.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Algorithmic Authorship & Academic Integrity
task_2_discursive.prompt: With the rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence in academic and literary writing, educational institutions are divided on policy. Some educators advocate for total prohibition to safeguard original critical thinking, while others argue that AI literacy and critical prompt engineering should become foundational curricular requirements. Write an essay evaluating both perspectives and present your reasoned stance on how educational bodies should respond.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Urban Density vs. Suburban Expansion
task_2_discursive.prompt: Faced with severe housing shortages, municipal authorities must choose between constructing high-density vertical apartment towers within established city limits or approving low-density suburban developments on agricultural greenbelts. Write an analytical essay discussing the environmental, economic, and social consequences of both approaches, and argue which strategy provides a more sustainable future.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Mandatory Civic Service for School Leavers
task_2_discursive.prompt: Several nations are actively considering legislation requiring all secondary school graduates to complete one year of mandatory civic service—such as ecological conservation, elderly social care, or disaster relief infrastructure. Proponents assert this fosters social cohesion, while critics view it as an infringement on personal liberty and career progression. Write an essay exploring both sides and state your own view.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Corporate Sponsorship of Scientific Research
task_2_discursive.prompt: As state funding for university scientific research declines, corporate entities are increasingly financing high-stakes biomedical and technological inquiries. Some argue this drives vital rapid innovation, while others contend it inevitably introduces commercial bias and compromises research integrity. Write an essay analyzing both perspectives and provide your own reasoned conclusion.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Cultural Preservation vs. Global Modernity
task_2_discursive.prompt: Globalization and rapid digital connectivity are accelerating the homogenization of indigenous dialects, traditional rituals, and regional customs. Some cultural theorists argue that preserving endangered languages and customs through state subsidies is essential, while others maintain that cultural evolution and integration are natural and beneficial. Write an essay evaluating both perspectives.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Remote Work and Civic Disengagement
task_2_discursive.prompt: The normalization of remote and home-based employment has drastically reduced commuting times and allowed greater personal flexibility. However, sociologists warn that eliminating physical workplace communities weakens broader civic participation, public transit viability, and downtown commerce. Write an essay discussing the broader societal trade-offs of the remote work revolution.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: The Monetization of Digital Privacy
task_2_discursive.prompt: Tech corporations defend targeted advertising models by noting that personalized advertising allows vital digital services, search engines, and communication tools to remain completely free for consumers. Critics counter that pervasive biometric and behavioral data harvesting poses existential risks to personal autonomy and democratic discourse. Write an essay evaluating both arguments.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Tourism Taxation and Heritage Protection
task_2_discursive.prompt: To combat over-tourism, several historic cities have implemented steep daily entry levies and hotel surcharges on international visitors. Advocates assert this curbs environmental wear and funds conservation, whereas tourism operators argue it penalizes ethical travelers and harms local businesses. Write an essay analyzing both sides and present your recommendation.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Automation of Public Judicial Decisions
task_2_discursive.prompt: Some legal theorists argue that utilizing artificial intelligence to assist judicial sentencing could eliminate human racial and socioeconomic bias in the courtroom. Conversely, civil liberties organizations argue that justice fundamentally demands human empathy, situational intuition, and accountability. Write an essay evaluating both arguments and state your own view on algorithmic legal adjudication.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Space Exploration Funding vs. Terrestrial Renewal
task_2_discursive.prompt: Billions of dollars are allocated annually by governments and private enterprises to deep-space exploration and lunar colonization missions. Critics argue this capital should be redirected exclusively toward urgent terrestrial challenges such as climate mitigation, clean water infrastructure, and poverty relief. Write an essay analyzing both perspectives and give your conclusion.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: The Future of Printed Books in the Digital Era
task_2_discursive.prompt: Despite the ubiquitous convenience of digital e-readers and audiobooks, global sales of physical printed volumes remain remarkably resilient. Some commentators argue that physical books will eventually become obsolete luxury relics, while others maintain that print offers irreplaceable cognitive, tactile, and aesthetic value. Write an essay examining both views.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Compulsory Nutritional Education in Primary Curriculums
task_2_discursive.prompt: With pediatric obesity and lifestyle-related diabetes increasing globally, public health authorities have proposed making comprehensive nutritional cooking and agricultural education mandatory in all primary schools. Opponents argue that schools are already overburdened with academic core subjects and that dietary habits belong strictly to parental discretion. Write an essay discussing both viewpoints.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Preservation of Historical Architecture in Modern Metropolises
task_2_discursive.prompt: In rapidly growing cities, older historical structures are frequently demolished to make way for high-capacity modern transit corridors and residential towers. Advocates for development argue modern housing needs must take precedence over sentimentality, while preservationists assert that architectural heritage forms the spiritual and cultural anchor of urban identity. Write an essay on this debate.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Universal Basic Income in the Era of Robotic Automation
task_2_discursive.prompt: As automation and sophisticated machine learning systems threaten widespread displacement of white-collar and blue-collar professions, economists are debating Universal Basic Income (UBI). Proponents claim UBI guarantees human dignity and spurs creative entrepreneurship, while opponents warn of unsustainable fiscal deficits and diminished work incentives. Write an essay assessing this issue.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Compulsory Second Language Learning in Early Childhood
task_2_discursive.prompt: Cognitive neuroscientists demonstrate that learning a foreign language before age seven accelerates neuroplasticity and cross-cultural empathy. However, critics claim that early foreign language instruction overburdens young children who are still mastering their native language literacy. Write an essay exploring whether foreign language learning should be mandatory from early childhood.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Regulation of Fast Fashion Production and Environmental Tariffs
task_2_discursive.prompt: The global fast fashion industry generates millions of tons of textile waste and chemical effluent every year. Some environmental advocates propose introducing strict global carbon tariffs on low-cost synthetic clothing, while manufacturing industry bodies argue such taxes unfairly harm low-income consumers and developing economies reliant on garment exports. Write an essay evaluating this proposal.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: High-Stakes Standardized Testing in University Admissions
task_2_discursive.prompt: Many universities worldwide are moving away from standardized entry examinations, opting instead for holistic portfolios comprising interviews, personal statements, and extracurricular achievements. Proponents celebrate the reduction in student stress, while defenders of standardized tests argue they provide the only objective, meritocratic safeguard against grade inflation and nepotism. Write an essay on this reform.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: The Role of Public Subsidies for Independent Journalism
task_2_discursive.prompt: As commercial advertising revenues shift almost entirely to digital tech monopolies, independent investigative journalism faces unprecedented financial collapse. Some democratic theorists advocate for public government subsidies to preserve investigative newsrooms, whereas skeptics argue state funding inevitably compromises press independence and editorial impartiality. Write an essay analyzing this dilemma.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: The Ethical Boundaries of Genetic Modification in Agriculture
task_2_discursive.prompt: Genetically modified crops engineered for drought tolerance and pest resistance could protect vulnerable populations against climate-induced famines. However, environmental bioethicists warn that modified organisms risk disrupting wild ecosystems and entrenching corporate monopolies over global seed supplies. Write an essay discussing the ethical balance between food security and ecological caution.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Decoupling Economic Growth from Resource Consumption
task_2_discursive.prompt: Traditional economic models correlate national prosperity with continuous Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth. However, ecological economists argue that infinite growth on a finite planet is structurally impossible, advocating for steady-state or 'degrowth' paradigms that prioritize human well-being over material expansion. Write an essay examining whether sustained economic growth remains compatible with planetary survival.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: The Privatization of Public Healthcare Systems
task_2_discursive.prompt: Proponents of private healthcare argue that competition and market incentives stimulate clinical innovation, modernize medical technologies, and reduce surgical waiting times. Conversely, champions of state-funded universal healthcare argue that medical care is a fundamental human right that must never be subordinated to corporate profit margins. Write an essay evaluating both perspectives.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Restricting Private Automobile Access in City Centers
task_2_discursive.prompt: To combat urban carbon emissions and air pollution, several European capitals have banned or heavily taxed private passenger vehicles in central metropolitan districts. Supporters report dramatic decreases in pedestrian accidents and respiratory illnesses, while suburban commuters argue such bans penalize those without access to reliable public rail networks. Write an essay analyzing both sides.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: The Social Implications of Cashless Societies
task_2_discursive.prompt: The transition toward an entirely cashless economy accelerates transaction efficiency and curtails financial crime and black-market tax evasion. However, privacy advocates and social workers warn that cashless systems exclude the unbanked and elderly while granting financial institutions unprecedented surveillance powers over citizen spending. Write an essay discussing whether society should eliminate physical cash.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Intellectual Property Rights and Essential Pharmaceuticals
task_2_discursive.prompt: During global public health emergencies, pharmaceutical conglomerates argue that strict patent protections are essential to recoup billions invested in clinical trials and stimulate future biomedical research. Global health advocates counter that monopolies on life-saving medicines cost thousands of preventable deaths and that patents must be waived for developing nations. Write an essay on this conflict.

task_2_discursive.title: Task 2: Regulating Micro-Targeted Political Advertising on Social Platforms
task_2_discursive.prompt: Micro-targeted digital advertising allows political campaigns to tailor messaging to individual psychological profiles, potentially mobilizing disengaged voters. Yet critics argue it fragments public political debate, spreads covert disinformation, and manipulates democratic election outcomes. Write an essay evaluating whether governments should ban micro-targeted political advertising.
